Surah al-Dukhan is among the Ha-Mim surahs. That is, the ones that begin with the disjointed letters (Ha-Mim). We have already discussed these letters at a length that makes repeating it here unnecessary. These letters bring the intellect to a halt at the point of pronouncing them as they are, as the Messenger of God (ﷺ) pronounced them. We do not ask ourselves about their meanings, and the intellect is not forbidden from hovering around them, attempting to derive some meanings, even if only to convince ourselves of something of the truth about their meanings, and then we say: God knows best what He intends by them.

This is because religion contains matters related to belief ('aqidah), matters related to rulings (ahkam), and matters related to the Qur'an, which expresses belief and rulings.

In each of these three there is an unseen (ghayb) and a witnessed (mashhad) dimension. The unseen is entrusted to knowledge of God, Exalted, so that a person remains powerless before the knowledge of God and before matters he does not understand, yet believes in them simply because God has informed of them in His Book, or on the tongue of His Messenger (ﷺ), who "does not speak from desire."

In matters of belief, for example, the belief in one God is unseen, but the intellect can furnish evidence for it, because if there were in them (the heavens and the earth) gods other than God, they would both have been corrupted. And if there were multiple gods, each specializing in some part of creation, each one would be in need of the others and none would be fit to be a god.

So: by reason we can establish that God is one God. But in matters of belief there are unseen matters into which the intellect cannot intervene, and in which one stops at what one has heard, such as: the grave, the barzakh (intermediate state), the reckoning, and the Hereafter.

Likewise in rulings there is unseen and witnessed. Prayer, in its visible aspect, establishes a servant's direction of worship in the universe: when we hear "Allahu Akbar" we go to the mosques and stand before our Lord, bowing and prostrating, with the leader and the led, the rich and the poor, the strong and the weak all equal in this, all humbled before God.

This is the witnessed side of prayer. In it there is also an unseen dimension in which reason has no role. As for prayer in terms of the number of its units (rak'at), it is unseen, and we do not know an explanation for it. Why was the dawn prayer two units, the noon prayer four, and the sunset prayer three? Therefore the question that revolves around the number of units is a false question.

The same applies to the Qur'an: it contains an unseen into which reason has no access, namely these disjointed letters, whose knowledge we leave to their Speaker, glorified and exalted is He.

Thus the Truth, glorified is He, at the opening of this surah combined the unseen in (Ha-Mim) and the witnessed in ﴿وَٱلْكِتَابِ ٱلْمُبِينِ﴾ [al-Dukhan: 2]; both are from God, so there is no oath upon this.

Even if we look at engineering principles and theories, we find that they rely at their beginning on a self-evident matter existing in the universe.

So: every advancement in the universe came from a self-evident matter bestowed by Allah, and the work of the intellects on self-evident matters is part of developing the earth.

Therefore, when you reflect on the Qur'an's style in addressing people, you find it begins with simple matters far from intellectual complexity: it speaks to them first about the foundation of the method by which their lives are set right and their movements in life harmonized, and it addresses the intellects in a way suited to their intellectual development.

When human thought matures and the method takes hold among people in conduct and practice, it begins to speak to them about rational theories and says to them: the earth is spherical, and it revolves around the sun, because intellects have by then become prepared for research and investigation.

Consider, for example, roads, and how they were primitive, merely a path in the desert wide enough for a single camel. And how they have developed now, with what has become available of the means of comfort, safety, speed, and security and others. It is the intellect when it works to advance.

Did man not learn from the crow how to bury the dead? Did we not learn from dogs, and use them now despite scientific advancement, in tracking traces and identifying criminals using the sense of smell? So: we took the natural matters which God bestowed upon us, built upon them, and developed them for the building of the earth.

And the building of the earth does not stand unless the method is first set right, for it is the foundation of advancement and the foundation of reform, because when the Creator, glorified is He, created creation, He made for it a method that governs it and regulates its movement in life: do this and do not do that.

If it is upright upon the method of its Lord and Creator, its life is set right; and if it deviates and departs, the nakedness of society appears and signs of corruption creep through its joints.

We have previously illustrated this with the "manual" (the catalogue) which the maker provides to protect his creation and maintain it: likewise, if you walk upon the method of your Creator, no ruin will ever befall you. From here came the mission of the messengers: for clarification and for reminding of the method ("do this" and "do not do that"). Even Adam, what happened to him when he opposed the method? Our Lord said to him: "Eat from the garden as you wish, except this tree," and they both ate from it. What happened?

When he opposed, ruin befell him, and his nakedness appeared when he ate from the tree, and he was compelled to something he had not known before: the release of wind and excrement and the disturbance of the stomach, matters he had not felt before the transgression.

And His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Indeed, We were ever sending [messengers]﴾ [al-Dukhan: 5], meaning: sending messengers to those whom We made successors on the earth, so that the movement of life is saved from ruin, and so that society is saved from evils, and so that it supports one another and does not conflict.

The matter of "revelation" (inzal) means sending something down from above to below, and it entails: a sender (munzil), a thing sent (munzal), and a recipient (munzal ilayh). The one who sent it down is Allah, and since the sender is Allah, the sending is from the direction of height, setting aside the question of place, because He said about iron: ﴿And We sent down iron, wherein is mighty strength and benefits for mankind﴾ [al-Hadid: 25], and iron is in the depths of the earth; sending down (inzal) implies the elevation of the one who sends.

Then the thing sent down is the Noble Qur'an: ﴿We sent it down﴾ [al-Dukhan: 3], to the one who was sent it down to mankind, ﴿in a blessed night﴾ [al-Dukhan: 3], which is the Night of Power (laylat al-Qadr), meaning: the time of the general revelation of the Qur'an.

He said ﴿in a night﴾ [al-Dukhan: 3] because the night is the place of stillness and calm, where there is no noise, no clamour, and no uproar that could distract the one to whom it is revealed; likewise, the human being is at rest, with his limbs not occupied with anything.

So: at night, the intellect is endowed with all the means of attention, comprehension, and purity of soul. Therefore, read at the beginning of Surat al-Muzzammil: ﴿O you wrapped in garments! Stand (in prayer) through the night, except a little, half of it, or subtract from it a little, or add to it, and recite the Qur'an distinctly (tartil). Indeed, We are going to cast upon you a weighty word. Indeed, the rising at night is more effective for concentration and more suitable for words﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 1-6].

So: the Qur'an was revealed at night because it is the most suitable time for its revelation, and it was revealed upon the heart of the Messenger of Allah in Makkah. Thus it is the night of Makkah and no other, and Makkah is the middle and center of the world, for which reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And thus We have made you a middle nation that you may be witnesses over the people and the Messenger a witness over you﴾ [al-Baqarah: 143].

Some said of this night that it is the Night of Power, based on His saying: ﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree﴾ [al-Qadr: 1]. Others said: rather, it is the night of the middle of Sha'ban. This matter needs for us to examine it carefully, because it was revealed in one of them.

We say: before the Qur'an was sent down and began its task in existence, where was it? It was in the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz): ﴿Indeed, it is a noble Qur'an, in a Book well-guarded, which none touches except the purified﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 77-79], and He said: ﴿And indeed, it is in the Mother of the Book with Us, exalted and wise﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 4].

So the first revelation of the Qur'an was in one whole piece from the Preserved Tablet to the lowest heaven. But did what was recorded in the Preserved Tablet descend, or a copy of it? They said: rather, a copy of it after it was transcribed.

Then after that it was revealed in portions (munajjaman) according to circumstances and events. The angel Jibril brought it down upon the heart of our master, the Messenger of Allah, each portion of it in a particular occasion.

So: we have three stages of the revelation of the Qur'an. The first: its transcription from the Preserved Tablet, which has a time. Then its revelation in one whole piece to the lowest heaven, which has a time. Then its revelation in portions according to circumstances, and this revelation has a time extended over the course of events, lasting several years.

It is possible to find in these three stages a way out of the difficulty: is it in the Night of Power or in the middle of Sha'ban? There is no objection to both nights sharing this excellence at any stage of its stages.

Moreover, the night of the middle of Sha'ban has its own honour and distinction, which is the matter of the change of the qibla, which is the direction of all Muslims in every part of the earth. Then the orientation toward Bayt al-Maqdis had its time and its wisdom, and then the change to the Ka'bah also had its time and its wisdom.

So the comparison here is not between truth and falsehood, but between two wise matters; but this has its time and that has its time. Therefore, the Almighty did not will to make the change of the qibla at the start of an obligation, but rather, during the obligation He divided the command of the change into two parts: he prayed half of the first prayer toward Bayt al-Maqdis and half of it toward the Ka'bah.

If this indicates anything, it indicates that Bayt al-Maqdis is among the sanctities of the Muslims just as the Ka'bah is entirely, and the incident of the Isra' from Bayt al-Maqdis confirms that.

So: Allah the Exalted willed that the direction of prayer be sometimes toward Bayt al-Maqdis and sometimes toward the Ka'bah, for a wisdom in both. The first: that Bayt al-Maqdis be among the sanctities of the Muslims. The second: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had an attachment to the qibla of Ibrahim (peace be upon him).

Therefore Allah the Exalted said: ﴿We have certainly seen the turning of your face toward the sky, so We will surely turn you to a qiblah with which you will be pleased. So turn your face toward al-Masjid al-Haram...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 144].

And prayer was enjoined upon the Messenger of Allah after his ascension to the heaven from Bayt al-Maqdis, and this prayer has within it the direction of the qibla, so the qibla must take both: the legislative principle and the preservative principle. And this He made a trial for the Muslims and for non-Muslims, because when the qibla was toward Bayt al-Maqdis they said: what turned him from the qibla of Ibrahim to the qibla of Dawud and Sulayman? And we said: so that you enter into the sanctities of Islam and they do not exclusively claim them.

The Jews seized this matter and made it a doubt, and they said: if Muhammad rejects our religion, how does he follow our qibla? So it was a trial for both parties, so that the human being adheres to the divine directives without the intellect intervening in them.

They said of the blessed night: it is the Night of Acquittal (laylat al-Bara'ah), the Night of the Document (laylat al-Sakk), and the Night of Mercy. The Night of Acquittal is derived from the acquittal (bara'ah) that the zakat collector used to give to the wealth-owner when he paid him God's right in his wealth, which is zakat: the collector gives him a certificate of acquittal (sakk al-bara'ah) indicating his payment of zakat and the clearing of his obligation from it; and the sakk has the same meaning.

As for the Night of Mercy, they said: a mercy upon the Messenger of Allah ﷺ first, because his soul yearned to turn toward the qibla of Ibrahim.

We have already said: suppose someone throws an apple at you, and at the same time another throws a stone at you; which of them will you concern yourself with? There is no doubt that you are keen first to ward off the stone from yourself, and you prioritize that over receiving the apple.

Likewise is the situation in this Qur'anic style: ﴿Indeed, We were ever warners﴾ [al-Dukhan: 3]. The word (kunna, "We were") indicates the past, although the warning is continuous and still ongoing, because the Exalted is not bound by a specific time, since He is the Creator of time, and as long as time is among the creation of Allah, the created cannot control the Creator.

So the past, present, and future are with respect to us human beings; but with respect to Allah the Exalted, all time is equal. When you read, for example, ﴿And Allah was ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Ahzab: 50], you say: He was, and still is, and will be in the future, because since He was in eternity, and He is not subject to change, He is forgiving and merciful from eternity to eternity.

And reflect on the description of the matter itself as (wise), because it is a command of Allah ﴿a command from Us﴾ [al-Dukhan: 5], meaning: there is no wisdom that rises to the level of this matter which comes from the Exalted; ﴿Indeed, We were ever sending [messengers]﴾ [al-Dukhan: 5], meaning: We did not leave Our creation neglected; rather We created them and sent to them those who take them by the hand to the straight path, guide them to right guidance, and make clear to them.

Translation of the passage:

That is: sending (the messengers) is a mercy from God toward His servants, because it is a command given to us by one who is above us, and we find no humiliation in that; none of us looks down upon the other, because we receive our commands from God...

So: life is set right for us when we walk upon the method (manhaj). Therefore He named it (al-Sirat al-Mustaqim, the Straight Path) and named it (sawa' al-sabil, the even way), meaning: it is in the middle, it does not incline to this side or that, because He wants to spare you effort and spare you time. All of this is the fruit of the method and of walking upon the Straight Path.

This is a mercy from God toward us. Yes, a mercy toward us that He does not leave us to trial, with some of us surging into others until we reach what is correct, the truth, and the Straight Path. Among His mercy toward us is that He does not leave us contending and colliding with one another; rather He made laws for us and made for us a method to walk upon from the beginning of the road.

There is a difference between a command that forces you to correct your course and a command that is balanced from the start. Among God's mercy toward us is that He makes us walk in one direction, such that all movements are in the direction of building, and all efforts toward one goal, in which all individuals cooperate and all individuals support one another.

Otherwise, if the movements were colliding, they would demolish and destroy. What is the benefit of your building while others demolish?... Reflect on the wording of the Qur'an: ﴿A mercy from your Lord﴾ [al-Dukhan: 6], and it did not say "a mercy from God," because the Rabb (Lord) is the one who undertakes nurturing and care. We have previously said that divinity (al-uluhiyya) is obligation (taklif) and lordship (al-rububiyya) is bestowal ('ata'). So this mercy is the mercy of the Lord, the caring, merciful Nurturer, like a mother who raises her small child, tenderly embraces him, and strengthens him.

Since He, glory be to Him, is your Lord, your Nurturer and your Creator, it was incumbent upon you to obey Him and not to depart from His method. ﴿Indeed He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾: All-Hearing of all the pains and complaints of people, if they voice them, and All-Knowing ('Alim) of their conditions and what stirs in their breasts if they conceal it within themselves. Although the address here is in the singular form and directed to our master the Messenger of God.

﴿A mercy from your Lord﴾: that is, O Muhammad. This is a special care from God for His Messenger and an explanation of his station (ﷺ) with God. The eye of God watches over him, and it is dear to Him that harm or pain from his people should reach him; he is the most beloved of mankind to Him. Therefore He raised him with the upbringing that makes him not only guided in himself but also a guide (hadiyan) to people.

Following the statement of the Exalted, ﴿a mercy from your Lord﴾ [Ad-Dukhan: 6], He reinforced it with His words, ﴿Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them﴾ [Ad-Dukhan: 7], and then returned the matter to their own certainty: ﴿if you are certain﴾ [Ad-Dukhan: 7], as if He were confident that, when they are questioned, they will say nothing but this. So, since you are certain that Allah is the Creator of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them, why did you deny His Messenger?!

The cosmic signs are clear in indicating their Creator, Mighty and Majestic. This sky that shades you, this earth that carries you, and what lies between them of bounties and secrets, and even what is beneath the soil of treasures, all point to Allah. If this which we see in the earth and the sky is the world of dominion (ʿĀlam al-Mulk), then what of the world of the unseen sovereignty (ʿĀlam al-Malakūt)?

The world of dominion is something you can perceive with your senses, but the world of sovereignty (Malakūt) is unseen, and we know of it only what Allah has told us, as He said, Exalted, concerning our master Ibrahim: ﴿And thus We showed Ibrahim the sovereignty of the heavens and the earth..﴾ [Al-An'am: 75].

As for His words ﴿if you are certain﴾ [Ad-Dukhan: 7], certainty (al-yaqīn) is receiving a matter without doubt, whether by knowledge, by sight, or by reality, as we explained earlier concerning knowledge of certainty (ʿilm al-yaqīn), then eye of certainty (ʿayn al-yaqīn), then truth of certainty (ḥaqq al-yaqīn). Certainty is thus the firm conviction that does not change, by judging it in existence through knowledge, sight, and reality.

These three stages are mentioned in His words, Exalted: ﴿No! If you knew with the knowledge of certainty, you would surely see the Blazing Fire. Then you would surely see it with the eye of certainty. Then you will surely be questioned that Day about the pleasure [you indulged in]﴾ [At-Takathur: 5-8].

He said in Surat al-Waqi'ah: ﴿But if he is of the deniers, the astray, then for him is a welcome of boiling water, and burning in Hellfire. Indeed, this is the true certainty. So exalt the name of your Lord, the Mighty﴾ [Al-Waqi'ah: 92-96].

But were these people truly certain that Allah is the Lord of the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them? The Qur'an tells them: ﴿if you are certain﴾ [Ad-Dukhan: 7], and here "in" (in) implies doubt about their certainty, for if they were certain, they would have believed in the Messenger of Allah and affirmed him. They acknowledge that Allah is their Creator and the Creator of the whole universe, yet they clashed with the religion of Allah. Why?

Because the religion restrains their movement and deprives them of desires and of benefiting from the corruption present in their society; the true religion deprives them of dominance and places them on equal footing with masters and slaves. Thus, they disliked the true religion because of the methodology it brought, and they inclined toward a false religion because it is devoid of methodology, having no commands and no prohibitions.

The Exalted One wants our speech to be reflected in our actions. The word ﴿There is no god﴾ [al-Dukhan: 8]: al-ilah (the deity) is the true object of worship. When they worshipped idols, they named them gods. Yes, gods by their own assumption and in their own imagination, but they were false gods and a false name, because the ilah is the one who is truly worshipped, who has a method (manhaj), and for whom there is proof.

As for their claim, it has no proof. It is only a form of worship that satisfies what is in their souls of an inclination toward religiosity, even if the object of worship is an idol that imposes no obligations and has no method.

Religiosity, as we have said, is a natural disposition (fitrah) in human beings, and reality and experience confirm this. When a person's means are constricted, even the disbeliever says, "O Lord," and turns to the true object of worship without deceiving himself, because the hardship that has befallen him, he knows, has no remover except God.

For this reason, no one has said, "O Lat, O 'Uzza." But unfortunately, when God removes their affliction and relieves their distress, they return to what they were doing. The Qur'an has often spoken on this theme. The Exalted said: ﴿When harm touches man, he calls upon Us, lying on his side, or sitting, or standing. But when We remove his harm from him, he continues on as if he had never called upon Us to remove a harm that touched him. Thus is made attractive to the wasteful what they used to do﴾ [Yunus: 12].

People forget that when religion restricts your movement in what is impermissible, you, as an individual, are restricting the movement of all people for your sake. It says to you: "Do not steal from people," and it says to all people: "Do not steal from you." So you are the first beneficiary of applying God's method.

After He said ﴿There is no god but He﴾ [al-Dukhan: 8], He gave the proof for it: ﴿He gives life and causes death﴾ [al-Dukhan: 8], because the matter of giving life and causing death belongs to God alone, with no rival in it. Those who enjoy life are not disturbed in the pleasure of this enjoyment except that they see death circling around them and about to strike them.

So, the Exalted has here addressed the thing that is most beloved to people. The one who owns your life and owns your death is God, so it does not befit you to be heedless of Him, or to turn away from His method and path to the path of another.

His saying ﴿He gives life and causes death﴾ [al-Dukhan: 8] is an action that actually falls upon others, although it is also among His attributes that He is Living and Self-Subsisting (al-Qayyum), as in the Verse of the Throne: ﴿God—there is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Subsisting﴾ [al-Baqarah: 255]. Some say that al-Hayy (the Living) is the Greatest Name of God, because it is the root, and every other attribute or name is a branch of it.

They said: al-Hayy is the Greatest Name in terms of giving, and Allah is the Greatest Name in terms of servitude, because the meaning of the word Allah is the one who is worshipped and obeyed in all His commands.

Since He is obeyed in all His commands, when you ask God, you say, "In the name of God," meaning: "In the name of God I proceed with this work," because work requires energy, requires a mind that thinks before you begin the work, and requires wisdom.

From whom do you draw these things? From God, because He alone gathers all the attributes of perfection and bestows upon you from His attributes. It is therefore obligatory to seek His help and rely upon Him. The one who said that the Greatest Name is al-Hayy looked to giving, and the one who said Allah looked to obligation.

As for His saying, glorified is He: ﴿your Lord and the Lord of your earliest forefathers﴾ [al-Dukhan: 8], He intended to argue against the disbelievers contemporary with the Messenger, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: ﴿We found our fathers upon a religion, and we are following in their footsteps﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 23]. So He wished to show their falsehood in this statement. If they were truly following the forefathers, they would have walked on the method of Adam, peace be upon him. But they deviated from it and departed from his guidance until the discourse of religion changed, and God's messengers multiplied to guide them.

The Most High, Glorified be He, here combines two attributes for them: that they are in doubt concerning the religion of God, and that they are playing, meaning: not serious about this matter. Even if only one of these two attributes were present, it would be sufficient to keep them away from the courtyard of faith.

﴿They are in doubt﴾... To understand the meaning of doubt (shakk), we say: the intellectual relations in propositions are six. Among them:

Knowledge (ʿilm): that you believe a proposition that reality supports.
Ignorance (jahl): that you believe a proposition that contradicts reality.
Imitation (taqlid): that you believe a proposition without being able to provide evidence for it, like a child who imitates his father and says, "God is One," but cannot establish the proof for it.
Then doubt (shakk): that two matters are equal in your mind, with neither preferred over the other. If you prefer one of them, then the preferred one is opinion (zann), and the non-preferred one is illusion (wahm).

Doubt, then, is that disbelief and belief are equal in their minds. And it is not only that they are in doubt, but also ﴿they are playing﴾. Had they been in doubt while earnestly searching and reflecting, they would have reached the truth. But they are jesting and playing, having no eagerness to reach the truth.

Al-Sha'rawi's commentary on Surah 44, verses 10–12:

The Truthful and Majestic (al-Haqq subhanahu) explains that He will not leave these doubters and deniers of His Messenger, who are heedless and playful, and that there is a Day for them on which He will exact retribution from them. So He says to the Messenger (ﷺ): ﴿So watch for them﴾ [al-Dukhan: 10], wait, ﴿the Day when the sky will bring forth a visible smoke﴾ [al-Dukhan: 10], i.e., a smoke that is manifest and dense.

Smoke (al-dukhan) consists of gases that intermingle and fill the atmosphere, like the morning mist (al-shubbura) that we see in the early hours. Because of its density, it leads to obstruction of vision, since the intermingling of its particles fills the gaps through which the eye could see. Then it causes constriction in the air and in breathing. So if you combine the lack of vision with the constriction of breath, you find that the distress is immense, which no human can bear.

It has been said: the smoke here is an indication of the drought that afflicted them and the famine that befell them, because when they went to extremes in denying the Messenger of Allah and intensified in harming him and his companions, he invoked (Allah) against them, and [it] said: famine and drought struck them, until they ate carrion and dead dogs, until they ate al-'ilhiz, which is wool or fur mixed with dried blood. This continued until they cried out and went to the Messenger of Allah asking him to supplicate to Allah to remove from them what had befallen them.

Allah has made clear to His Messenger their lying: if We were to remove the punishment from them, they would surely return to what they were upon of disbelief and denial.

The meaning of ﴿It covers the people﴾ [al-Dukhan: 11] is: it encompasses them and envelops them. ﴿This is a painful punishment﴾ [al-Dukhan: 11], because it prevents them from seeing and constricts their breathing, so they cry out. ﴿Our Lord, remove from us the punishment; indeed, we are believers﴾ [al-Dukhan: 12]. Allah knows that they are lying in this statement.

Therefore He says after it:

﴿How will there be for them the reminder...﴾.

﴿Indeed, We will lift the punishment a little; indeed you will return to disbelief.﴾

That is: the punishment of this world that befell them, which the Qur'an called "the lesser punishment": ﴿And We will surely make them taste the lesser punishment, short of the greater punishment, so that they may return﴾ [al-Sajdah: 21]. We will lift from them the punishment of the smoke, the famine and the hunger that compelled them to eat carrion. We will lift it from you a little, in order to prove to you that you are liars, even if only before yourselves, so that you may be convinced of this reality; for the believers in Me know it and bear witness to it, whereas you deny it.

Or, their lying is exposed before the young generation. Among them are those in whom disbelief has not taken firm root, so this causes a shaking in their ranks, and the disbelievers are revealed as they truly are, so their children, who follow these events and witness the lying of the fathers and grandfathers, do not imitate them.

Indeed, we have indeed seen among the sons of disbelievers those who embraced Islam and acquitted themselves well in Islam, such as ʿIkrimah ibn Abi Jahl and others, who saw with their own eyes the lying of their fathers and their lack of fidelity toward God.

Meaning: remember this day and do not be heedless of it. ﴿On the day when We shall seize with the greatest seizing; indeed, We will take vengeance.﴾ *Al-batsh* (البطش) means seizing with force, and a strong blow that takes hold of all the limbs of the body, without regard to which limb it strikes. We say: "Fulan *batasha* bi-Fulan," meaning he struck him harshly and violently, without regard to which part of him the blow fell upon. After this description, He called it "*al-Kubra*" (الكبرى, "the greatest"), to emphasise its severity and its harshness upon the disbelievers.

﴿Indeed, We will take vengeance.﴾ *Al-intiqam* (الانتقام, vengeance) implies a correspondence. So the seizing is not an aggression on Our part, but a recompense for what you had committed of denial and harm against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

The seizing, then, is a recompense of the same kind as the deed. Had it not been for this seizing, the justice of heaven would not have been realised between the believers and the disbelievers, and there would have been an equality between the believers who bore harm, hardship and persecution, and the disbelieving wrongdoers and transgressors.

This seizing had to befall the disbelievers so that the believers might see the fruit of their faith and how Allah saved them through their faith, so they rejoice; and so that the disbelievers might see the fruit of their disbelief and obstinacy, so they feel remorse, regret and pain.

In more than one place the Noble Qur'an relates to us a dialogue between the people of Paradise and the people of the Fire, which makes clear the joy of the believers and the regret and anguish of the disbelievers: ﴿The companions of the Fire will call out to the companions of Paradise: "Pour upon us some water, or some of what Allah has provided you." They will say: "Indeed, Allah has forbidden them both to the disbelievers."﴾ [al-A'raf: 50].

His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿Indeed, We will take vengeance.﴾ is an indication of the justice of heaven, as if Allah, may He be exalted, were saying to them: Do not blame Us for having seized you with this seizing, for you are Our making, and We are more compassionate toward you than a mother toward her child. But there must be retribution, so that the scales are balanced, and so that there is no fitnah (فتنة, trial and disorder).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 44, verses 17–18:

The word ﴿fatanna﴾ [al-Dukhan: 17] means: We tested and examined. Trial (fitna) is not blameworthy in itself; it is blamed only for its outcome, just as examination is neither praised nor blamed in itself, but according to what follows from it and what results from it.

That is because he would be confronted not with moral corruption or social corruption, but with corruption of belief ('aqadi).

It is as though God, exalted is He, is preparing him for his encounter with the head of disbelief, Pharaoh, whose misguidance reached the point where he claimed divinity and said to the people: I am your Lord, Most High.

From here, the mission of Musa (peace be upon him) was a difficult and arduous mission. Therefore his Lord, mighty and majestic, trained him in the use of the signs and miracles before he displayed them before Pharaoh.

Read: ﴿And what is that in your right hand, O Musa? He said: It is my staff; I lean upon it, and I beat down [leaves] with it for my sheep, and I have in it other uses. He said: Throw it down, O Musa. So he threw it, and suddenly it was a snake, moving swiftly﴾ [Ta-Ha: 17–20].

So the Truth, glorified is He, made Musa aware of the role of the staff in the doctrinal battle he would wage with Pharaoh, and trained him to deal with it, so that when he confronted Pharaoh he would face him with confidence, steadfastness, and assurance in God's victory and support. Therefore we have said that the orientalists seized upon this story and accused the Qur'an of repetition.

This indicates their lack of understanding of the verses in their context. The story of the staff indeed appears three times: once between Musa and his Lord, exo as training and practice on this matter; the second time before Pharaoh; and the third time before the sorcerers of Pharaoh.

So: each stage had its wisdom, and there is no repetition in the matter; rather, these are different situations, each in its appointed time.

As for His saying, glorified is He: ﴿That you deliver to me the servants of God﴾ [al-Dukhan: 18]. When you hear ﴿addu ilayya﴾ [al-Dukhan: 18], you know that there is a trust that must be discharged. So what is the trust that Musa asked his people to deliver to him?

They said: the right that Musa demanded of the people of Pharaoh is that he take the Children of Israel and bring them out from the humiliating punishment they suffer at the hands of Pharaoh's people. This is Musa's first mission; as for his call to Pharaoh, it was secondary to the main mission, and his speech with Pharaoh was beyond his mission and concerning the legislation he brought to the Children of Israel.

The reason for the persecution of the Children of Israel by Pharaoh's people was that when the Hyksos entered Egypt they spread corruption in it, and the Children of Israel used to aid and assist the Hyksos. When the Hyksos left Egypt, the Children of Israel were left with no enemy but them, so they persecuted them.

As the Qur'an relates: ﴿They slaughter your sons and spare your women﴾ [al-Baqarah: 49]. Thus our master Musa came originally to rescue the Children of Israel from punishment and to bring them out of Egypt.

The Truth, glorified and exalted is He, showed kindness to the Children of Israel because they were the believers at that time, while the others were idolaters.

So the meaning of ﴿addu ilayya ibad Allah﴾ [al-Dukhan: 18] is: give me the Children of Israel whom you are torturing, and leave me to myself.

Among the miracles of the Qur'an is that when it speaks of the ruler of Egypt, it calls him Pharaoh, except in the period of our master Yusuf (peace be upon him), where it calls him the King: ﴿And the king said: Indeed, I see seven fat cows being eaten by seven lean ones﴾ [Yusuf: 43].

It is established that the Hyksos, during their presence in Egypt, changed the title of Pharaoh and said (al-Malik, the King), and their presence in Egypt was in the days of our master Yusuf (peace be upon him).

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, I am to you a trustworthy messenger﴾ [al-Dukhan: 18], meaning: entrusted with my message from God, which I discharge as the discharge ought to be.

It also contains an allusion to nullifying their claimed divinity. That is, you know among yourselves that you are not gods, and that this claim is false; therefore he frightened them with the true God.

﴿And indeed I have sought refuge in my Lord and your Lord from your stoning me﴾ [al-Dukhan: 20]. That is, I have turned to Him and sheltered myself in Him from your harm. What happened after he sought refuge in Allah? Allah subjected to him a man from the people of Pharaoh who believed Moses and defended him.

Allah saved Moses and those with him, and destroyed Pharaoh and his armies. This is from the absoluteness of power, that it destroys and saves by one and the same thing, because things do not act of their own essence, but by the will of Allah.

His saying ﴿from your stoning me﴾ [al-Dukhan: 20] indicates that stoning existed among the earlier nations that denied their messengers.

So: every scene in this story demonstrates the perfect freedom of power, which operates in all things and transforms a thing into its opposite. Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 44, verses 25–27:

That is: after Allah drowned them, they left behind this bounty. (Kam) here is khabariyya, indicating abundance. ﴿Gardens﴾ [al-Dukhan: 25], meaning verdant orchards and groves, ﴿and springs﴾ [al-Dukhan: 25], meaning the springs of sweet water that flow through these orchards.

﴿And a noble station﴾ [al-Dukhan: 26]. Maqam, with a fatha on the mim, is the noun of place for standing (qiyam): if you were sitting and then stood up. Muqam, with a damma on the mim, is the noun of place for residing (iqamah), the place of dwelling. A muqam is not described as karim (noble) unless the one who dwells in it has all the means of comfort and ease, so the station itself carries nobility. That is, it gathers for its owner every means of good, whether he stands or sits.

It is as if goodness follows him, obedient to his commands, and this is only the case when he has followers and he is the one followed. These followers carry out his orders while he stands and while he sits.

When a person is sitting, sleeping or reclining, what makes him stand? A matter that befalls him and raises him up. This matter is of two kinds: either a good thing that gladdens him and draws him to rise toward it, like a beloved or a friend returning from absence, so he stands up for him; or a matter that grieves and alarms him, so he rises because of it.

The word (muqam) with a damma on the mim also occurs, meaning the place of residence, in the words of the Most High: ﴿Indeed, it is evil as a settlement and a station﴾ [al-Furqan: 66], and in His words: ﴿Abiding therein; excellent as a settlement and a station﴾ [al-Furqan: 76].

As for His words ﴿and bounty wherein they had been delighting﴾ [al-Dukhan: 27]: the word (ni'mah) with a fatha on the nun also occurs twice, as here, and it occurs with a kasra on the nun, as in ﴿Remember My bounty which I bestowed upon you...﴾ [al-Baqarah: 40], in 34 places, either singular or attributed to Allah; and it occurs as ni'mati, ni'matika and ni'matahu (for the third person).

The difference between them is that ni'mah with a kasra means what one enjoys, but it is to be noted that what is enjoyed are things external to the self. Sometimes the bounty exists and the ability to enjoy it exists; sometimes the bounty exists but the ability to enjoy it does not. As for na'mah with a fatha, it means the existence of the bounty together with the existence of the ability to enjoy it.

His words ﴿they had been delighting therein﴾ [al-Dukhan: 27] come from tafakkuh (enjoyment and pleasure), derived from fakihah (fruit), which indicates luxury, because among food there are essential necessities, the things on which the sustenance and continuance of life depend, and there is other food for luxury and pleasure, like fruit eaten after the meal.

These things eaten for luxury and pleasure can be dispensed with, since they are not necessities, as evidenced by the fact that many people do not know the eating of fruit while they are alive and provided for. Thus: they were in a state of ease of living and enjoyment, over and above the necessities.

Thus (it was): like this, God took it away from them and gave it to others. Had it merely been taken from them, it would have been lighter upon them; but it was taken from them and given to others, and this is more painful.

This verse shows that inanimate things have feelings: they love and hate, weep and rejoice. Feeling therefore exists in all creatures to the degree that each needs it. In human beings it remains, so you see a person love his child even if the child is dull or unruly, and this love continues with him, and he may show more tenderness to that child than to a well-behaved one.

Hence, when they asked a Bedouin, "Which of your sons do you love most?" he said, "The young one until he grows up, the absent one until he returns, and the sick one until he recovers."

As for animals, their feeling is in proportion to need. You see an animal protect and defend its young offspring, but once the young one grows up it leaves it as if it knows nothing of it, and even if the young one were slaughtered before it, it would feel nothing toward it, because its feeling is only as great as the young one's need for rearing.

Likewise inanimate things: Allah, glorified is He, elevates them and gives them feeling. Among this feeling is that the heavens and the earth did not weep over those who were destroyed for opposing the way of Allah.

For this reason Allah addressed inanimate things and placed them in the rank of people of enlightened understanding who comprehend and reason, as evidenced by Allah's giving the heavens, the earth and the mountains a choice regarding bearing the Trust: ﴿Indeed, We offered the Trust to the heavens and the earth and the mountains, but they refused to bear it and were apprehensive of it...﴾ [al-Ahzab: 72].

This shows that they have choice and reason. Some have said that the heavens and the earth are compelled and subjugated to worship. I say: No, rather everything in existence other than Allah was given a choice. Some of them relinquished their choice for the choice of their Lord, and their own will for the will of their Creator, and some of them chose to be free to choose, and that is the human being.

We have said: There is a difference between the time of undertaking and the time of performance. You guarantee the time of undertaking and trust it, but you do not guarantee the time of performance. Therefore, inanimate things were more objective than human beings in this matter, because they chose from the outset to be subjected to their Lord, whereas the human being chose to be one who chooses. At the time of performance, some of them believed and some disbelieved, some obeyed and some disobeyed.

If you say: In what language do the earth and the heavens speak, and how do they understand? We say: Their Creator, glorified is He, addresses them and understands from them, for He knows their language. Therefore Allah, the Exalted, gives us examples of the speech of these creatures and their glorification of Allah, the Exalted. He said: ﴿And We subjected the mountains to glorify [Allah] along with David, and the birds [as well]; and We were doing [that].﴾ [al-Anbiya: 79] And He said: ﴿And there is not a thing except that it exalts [Allah] by His praise, but you do not understand their [way of] exalting.﴾ [al-Isra: 44]

In the story of Sayyidina Sulayman (peace be upon him), the hoopoe spoke words that showed its knowledge and its understanding of the matter of monotheism in the best possible understanding, and an ant spoke, and we find with it the standards of truth and justice.

By Allah, a person is astonished when he reads His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Have you not considered that to Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth, and the sun and the moon and the stars and the mountains and the trees and the moving creatures and many of the people? But upon many, the punishment has been justified. And whoever Allah humiliates – for him there is no honorer. Indeed, Allah does what He wills.﴾ [al-Hajj: 18]

So all creatures glorify [Allah] without exception, except that the human being is the only creature that deviates from this glorifying system.

Therefore we have said: The creatures other than the human being were more understanding than him when they rejected being given a choice and relinquished their own will for the will of their Lord. So: Do not be deceived, O human being, and know that the creatures around you have a role and a station with Allah, and in them has been created the like of what has been created in you of understanding and feeling.

It has been related in the authentic hadith from our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), what supports this matter. He said about Uhud: And it is established that the mountain was moved by him and his companions, so he said to it, and he said: It is also established in the hadith that the earth weeps for the death of the believer and rejoices at the death of the disbeliever. The Arabs say (nabat bihi al-dar), meaning: he disliked it.

This is only because these inanimate things have understanding and reason in some manner, and they are entirely in harmony with the way of Allah. They are obedient and glorifying, so they love those among mankind who are of their own kind, and dislike those among them who deviate from the way of Allah and the matter of monotheism.

Hence, when Sayyidina Imam Ali (may Allah be pleased with him) was asked, "Do the heavens and the earth weep?" he said: "Yes. When a believer dies, two places weep for him: a place on the earth and a place in the heavens. As for his place on the earth, it is the place of his prostration or his prayer-place; and as for his place in the heavens, it is the ascent of his deeds." So there is a companionship between the place and the one who dwells in it, between the place and the believing human being.

With this we understand ﴿So the heaven and the earth did not weep for them﴾ [al-Dukhan: 29], and how could the heaven weep over the destruction of the enemy of Allah, Pharaoh, after he defied the Truth, the Exalted, and claimed that he was a god besides Allah?

And His saying: ﴿nor were they reprieved﴾ [al-Dukhan: 29] means: they were not delayed or postponed from their appointed time which Allah had set as their end, because when the term of Allah comes, it is not deferred.

ۿ"from the humiliating torment" (Qur'an 44:30). Torment (al-'adhab) is that which causes pain to the body, and it may be by fire or by other means, such as the cutting off of a part of the body or the skin, for example. To physical torment another torment may be added, which is moral: disgrace and humiliation. Some people can bear physical torment, but cannot bear that you humiliate them with a word, which may be more severe for them than torment.

The Children of Israel were suffering torment through the slaughter of their sons, and suffering humiliation through the sparing of their women (istihyaʾ, the sparing of women alive). Women are a point of weakness for a man, and a matter of honour (ʿird) that must be guarded; therefore, violating a man's women is the greatest humiliation to him.

Yet God, the Truth, glory be to Him, in His mercy, came to the aid of the Children of Israel and rescued them from the humiliating torment "from Pharaoh" (Qur'an 44:31). He was the cause of this torment.

The extravagant (musrif) is the one who exceeds the limit that God has set for him, to others. Pharaoh was arrogant, and extravagant in his arrogance. It is enough of his extravagance that he claimed divinity, saying to the people, "I am your lord, the Most High," and that he deceived his people and led them into delusion.

Pharaoh went astray and led an entire nation astray and enslaved it, and the saying of the one who said it is true: "Since when have you enslaved people, when their mothers bore them free?"

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 44, verse 32:

﴿And We certainly chose them over the worlds with knowledge.﴾

The discussion here concerns the Children of Israel. They hold fast to this verse and build upon it the claim that they are the "chosen people of God," saying: "The God who created you and sent to you a messenger is the One who chose us over the worlds."

This is a false claim, because the meaning of ﴿over the worlds﴾ [al-Dukhan: 32] is: the worlds of their own time, and their contemporaries among the people of Pharaoh and others. These were, for the most part, idolaters. God preferred the Children of Israel over them because they believed in God, and at that time they were the best of God's creation altogether.

But they wished to extend this ruling to all people, and to "the worlds" in every time and place. This is not permissible, as evidenced by the fact that when they opposed God's method, He broke them up into nations across the earth and scattered them everywhere as a punishment for them.

Indeed, you find in every country a quarter bearing their name, called (the Jewish Quarter), where you see them gathered together and closed in upon themselves, not blending in and not melting into the society around them.

The Qur'an expresses this very meaning in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And We divided them in the earth into nations﴾ [al-A'raf: 168]. Thus every group of them in one place represents a nation in itself, because they do not melt into other nations.

What negates their claim is His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And [remember] when your Lord proclaimed that He would surely send against them until the Day of Resurrection those who would afflict them with the worst torment﴾ [al-A'raf: 167]. This is what actually happens: from time to time, God sets over them those who inflict upon them the worst torment.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 44, verse 33:

His saying: ﴿And We gave them of the signs that which contained a clear trial﴾ [Ad-Dukhan: 33]. The signs are the miracles that accompanied the call of our master Musa (Moses), peace be upon him. By these signs Allah saved them from drowning and saved them from the people of Pharaoh.

What is remarkable is that as soon as Allah saved them from drowning and from Pharaoh, and as soon as they came out safe, they saw a people worshipping their idols, so they said to Musa, peace be upon him, ﴿Make for us a god just as they have gods﴾ [Al-A'raf: 138]. They committed shirk (associating partners with Allah), while their feet were still wet from crossing the sea.

During the period of wandering (al-tih), Allah honoured them and sent down upon them al-Mann and al-Salwa, which are among the finest of foods and the most delicious to eat. It came down to them without weariness and without effort. But because of their materialism, they objected to al-Mann and al-Salwa.

They said to Musa: ﴿We will not endure one kind of food, so call upon your Lord for us to bring forth for us from what the earth grows: its herbs, its cucumbers, its garlic, its lentils, and its onions.¦ He said: Would you exchange that which is lower for that which is better?..﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 61]. They desired a material thing that they handle themselves and whose source they know. Indeed, their materialism reached the point that they said to the Prophet of Allah, Musa: ﴿Show us Allah openly﴾ [An-Nisa: 153].

Some said: Musa, peace be upon him, was the one who opened this door when he said: ﴿My Lord, show me Yourself, that I may look upon You﴾ [Al-A'raf: 143].

The word ﴿balaʾ﴾ [Ad-Dukhan: 33] means a test and examination, to know their reactions after they saw the signs or after they saw the blessings. And we have said: trial and testing are neither blameworthy nor praiseworthy in themselves; rather, they are judged by the consequences that follow from them.

Commentary: The allusion in ﴿Indeed, these people would say﴾ [al-Dukhan: 34] may refer to the Children of Israel, because if you look into the Torah or the Talmud you will find nothing in them about the Last Day, even though it is a fundamental pillar of faith. They are a people who do not believe in this Day.

Their position, as the Qur'an relates their saying, is: ﴿The Fire will not touch us except for a few counted days﴾ [Al 'Imran: 24]. That is, after which it will go out from us and the matter will end. And in another verse they said: ﴿We are the children of God and His beloved﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 18].

Or these people may refer to deniers of resurrection in general, whether the Children of Israel or others. Their saying ﴿It is nothing but our first death﴾ [al-Dukhan: 35] means by "the first death" the non-existence that preceded creation. They consider non-existence to be a death, and then God created Adam, from whom came the rest of creation.

This is like the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And you were dead and He gave you life﴾ [al-Baqarah: 28]. That is, "We will not die except this one death, and there is no other death after it, no resurrection and no reckoning." ﴿And we will not be resurrected﴾ [al-Dukhan: 35], that is, raised alive after death.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 44, verse 36:

We have said that faith rests on the unseen matters (ayat al-ghayb): you believe in the existence of God, in Paradise and in Hell without seeing them. This is the place of faith. As for visible signs (al-ayat al-mushahada), there is no faith in them. You do not say, "I believe that the sun has risen." But these people, because of the materialism that governs them, want a sign of the unseen to be visible, so they say ﴿Then bring us our fathers, if you are truthful﴾ [al-Dukhan: 36], and there is no "where" with the eye.

They do not believe except in what is perceptible to the senses (al-amr al-hissi). Therefore they want their fathers to be restored after death so that they may believe that resurrection is true. We say to them: If you want that, then you have the books of history and the heavenly messages, which relate to you things like what you want, such as the story of al-Uzayr: ﴿Or like the one who passed by a town, fallen upon its roofs. He said, "How will Allah bring this to life after its death?" So Allah caused him to die for a hundred years; then He revived him. He said, "How long have you remained?" He said, "I have remained a day or part of a day." He said, "Rather, you have remained a hundred years. But look at your food and your drink; they have not spoiled. And look at your donkey. And We will make you a sign for the people. And look at the bones: how We raise them and then clothe them with flesh." And when it became clear to him, he said, "I know that Allah is over all things competent"﴾ [al-Baqara: 259].

Likewise in the story of the People of the Cave, whom God says Allah revived after three hundred and nine years. Also, the moment they rose from their sleep or death they said ﴿We have remained a day or part of a day﴾ [al-Mu'minun: 113], because this is the usual period of human sleep.

These and other events occurred in past times, and they know of those people and believe in them. Likewise in His saying: ﴿Have you not seen those who left their homes, being thousands, fearing death? Allah said to them, "Die," and then He brought them to life﴾ [al-Baqara: 243].

Those whom Allah revived after death live only to the extent of the miracle, and then they die. Therefore there is no proof for these people in demanding the revival of their fathers, since Allah did revive the dead and conveyed that through the tongues of the messengers, yet they did not believe. And even if Allah had revived their fathers for them, they would not have believed.

The Exalted Lord wants to compare these people with the nations before them that denied their messengers, and He says to them: you are no novelty in this, and you are not exempt from the fate that befell those who denied before you.

﴿Are they better...?﴾ [al-Dukhan: 37] meaning: the Children of Israel. ﴿Or the people of Tubba'?﴾ [al-Dukhan: 37] Tubba' al-Himyari, one of the kings of Yemen. Yemen was anciently called the Green Land, or Happy Yemen, because of its abundant bounty.

Tubba' was a righteous man, but his people opposed him and denied him, so God seized them with the seizure of the Mighty, the Omnipotent, after He destroyed the dam that supplied them with water for cultivation. With the destruction of the dam, their whole life was destroyed.

This story reminded me of the days when we were in Algeria. There they built a dam that holds back rainwater, and they named it the Dam of Ma'rib. When we went with the President to inaugurate it, one of them stood up to speak, and among what he said was: "Now the dam has been built, and you will water your land and your crops, whether the sky rains or not."

These words stopped me, and I saw in them a contradiction, not only to religion but also to reason and logic. So I said to their foreign minister: "Tell the honorable speaker: if the sky does not rain, what then will he or the dam hold back?"

His saying: ﴿Indeed they were criminals﴾ [al-Dukhan: 37]. The word mujrim (criminal) is only used of one who has gone to great lengths in disobedience and in committing sins, to a great extent. Mujrim means one who commits a gross offense. Here He spoke in general terms: ﴿And those before them, We destroyed﴾ [al-Dukhan: 37].

In another place He elaborated on this destruction, saying: ﴿So each We seized for his sin. Among them were those upon whom We sent a violent wind, and among them were those seized by the Blast, and among them were those whom We caused the earth to swallow, and among them were those whom We drowned...﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 40].

And in Surat al-Fajr: ﴿Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with 'Ad, Iram of the pillars, the like of which was never created in the lands, and Thamud who hewed the rocks in the valley, and Pharaoh, owner of the stakes?﴾ [al-Fajr: 6-10].

These were all nations that had civilizations, but their civilizations did not enable them to preserve them or to prevent them from vanishing, so that they ended as though they had never existed. The Exalted Lord used to seize the nations that denied with the seizure of the Mighty, the Omnipotent, because the earlier messengers were not commanded to fight; they were only required to convey the messages of God.

The heavens themselves undertook the chastisement of those who denied and the retribution against them. Fighting was not permitted except to our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), because he is the one trusted to lead mankind with his judgment, saturated with the method of God. For this reason no messenger came after him, and the fact that no messenger came after him is a testimony to the goodness of his community, and this goodness will remain within it until the Hour arrives.

﴿وَمَا خَلَقْنَا ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا لَـٰعِبِينَ﴾ [الدخان: ٣٨]

God, glorified and exalted, wants to draw attention to a cosmic matter that encompasses all time, past and present. This matter is the attribute of steadfastness in the creation of the heavens and the earth. Since God Most High created them, they have moved according to a precise order that does not deviate, change, or alter.

This steadfastness means that they were created upon truth and by truth. Truth is what is constant, while falsehood changes. For this reason we have said: if you look at a false witness before the judge, his statements are bound to contradict one another, and the investigator continues to question him until he falls into contradiction and exposes the falsehood that he tries to dress in the garb of truth.

Contradiction arises in his statements because he draws upon falsehood woven from his own imagination. But the one who draws upon truth and speaks it, his statements do not change as long as he holds fast to the truth. Truth is constant and is reality, so from where would contradiction come?

Investigators have methods and techniques by which they expose falsehood and reach the truth. For this reason they said: "If you are a liar, then be a good rememberer" (fa-kun dhakūran). But at some point memory is bound to betray you, and the tongue of truth is bound to prevail over the tongue of falsehood.

Let me mention, among us in Daqadous, one of the farmers, who was a boaster (fashshār). Once we were returning from the market town (al-Bandar), Mit Ghamr, and this friend of ours was recounting some of his stories. He said: "This happened on the night of the Little Eid, and the moon was shining at noon."

Glory be to God! How can the moon be shining at noon on the night of the Little Eid? Even ordinary people say in their proverbs: "Lies have no legs." Indeed.

The Truth here says: ﴿وَمَا خَلَقْنَا ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا لَـٰعِبِينَ﴾ [الدخان: ٣٨] meaning: We created them in earnest, not in play, and with truth, not with falsehood. In the verse after it He said: ﴿مَا خَلَقْنَاهُمَآ إِلاَّ بِٱلْحَقِّ﴾ [الدخان: ٣٩]. This steadfastness indicates precision in creation, that they were created with care, with exact and firm engineering, and with laws that do not conflict, from the time God created them until the Hour arrives.

Consider, for example, the sun in its risings and its settings, and its movement and speed relative to the earth. Consider the moon and the phenomena of its eclipses. All these signs occur with extreme precision and in balances that never deviate or conflict. Bring me any human machine that works and remains precise all the time.

He who created the heavens and the earth in a precise order whose creation does not conflict has a purpose, and this purpose has been the same since Adam, peace be upon him, until the end of the world.

We have said ﴿إِلاَّ بِٱلْحَقِّ..﴾ [الدخان: ٣٩], the constant thing that does not change. He, glorified, says: ﴿وَٱلسَّمَآءَ رَفَعَهَا وَوَضَعَ ٱلْمِيزَانَ * أَلاَّ تَطْغَوْاْ فِي ٱلْمِيزَانِ * وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلْوَزْنَ بِٱلْقِسْطِ وَلاَ تُخْسِرُواْ ٱلْمِيزَانَ﴾ [الرحمن: ٧-٩] (And the heaven He raised and set up the balance, that you not transgress within the balance, and establish weight with justice and do not make the balance deficient).

In this verse there is a subtle indication from God, glorified be He. He says: look at the sky and what is in it of stars and celestial bodies. Have you seen in it any defect or conflict? No, because it was created with truth, by the balance, and with precision as well. If you wish for the affairs of your lives to be balanced and upright, then take the balance of truth in all your lives, and then you will not find in society any contradiction or clash.

Because truth is constant, it is enduring and it is supreme. For this reason they said: "Truth is clear and falsehood is confused (lajlaj)." Truth is never effaced, even if falsehood rises over it for a while. God Most High allows falsehood a round in which it rises, until it bites people and makes them feel the importance of truth.

Thus falsehood itself is a soldier of truth's soldiers, and disbelief is a soldier of faith's soldiers. Had people not tasted the force and harshness of falsehood, they would not have known the sweetness of truth. For this reason, when faith came, none hastened to it more than those who suffered most from disbelief.

As for His saying: ﴿وَلَـٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لاَ يَعْلَمُونَ﴾ [الدخان: ٣٩] (but most of them do not know), they do not know these realities because they turn away from God's signs in the cosmos, turning away from reflection, as He, glorified, said: ﴿وَكَأَيِّن مِّن آيَةٍ فِي ٱلسَّمَاوَاتِ وَٱلأَرْضِ يَمُرُّونَ عَلَيْهَا وَهُمْ عَنْهَا مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ [يوسف: ١٠٥] (And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth they pass by, while they turn away from it).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1–53, fragments of 54–66) on surah 44, verses 40–42:

If they are turning away from Our signs in this world, then they will be made to face Us in the Hereafter, on the Day of Judgment (yawm al-fasl). ﴿Indeed, the Day of Judgment is the appointed time for them all﴾ [al-Dukhan: 40]. The Day of Resurrection is their appointed time, on which Allah gathers them all together: the follower and the followed, the believer and the disbeliever, the obedient and the disobedient, those who denied the messengers and those who affirmed them.

All will be gathered. ﴿The Day when no close friend will avail a close friend at all﴾ [al-Dukhan: 41]: no friend will benefit his friend, ﴿nor will they be helped﴾, and no relative will repel anything from his relative.

In another verse, He, glorified is He, says: ﴿Intimate friends on that Day will be enemies to one another, except the righteous﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 67]. Only the righteous remain, and their brotherhood and affection endure. As for friends who were bound together by the wealth and interests of this world, they will become enemies on the Day of Resurrection, each one casting the blame for his deeds upon his companion, because he saw him one day committing sin and did not restrain him from it nor advise him.

﴿Nor will they be helped﴾ [al-Dukhan: 41]: they will not find anyone who can help them besides Allah. ﴿Except for those on whom Allah has mercy﴾ [al-Dukhan: 42]. He showed them mercy first in this world, by rescuing them from disbelief, making them believers in Him and affirming His messenger, and by placing them upon His method and His straight path until they meet Him. This mercy is a preparation for the greatest mercy on the Day of Resurrection.

The word (mawla) is broad enough to include children, relatives, friends and close companions. Some people take slaves and servants, and every dependant of yours is included in it. All of these: ﴿no close friend will avail a close friend at all﴾ [al-Dukhan: 41], meaning he will not repel harm from him, nor bear his burden, because each one is preoccupied with himself, bearing his own load. This applies to human beings; likewise, idols will not benefit their worshippers, nor will any deity other than Allah.

Therefore Allah, the Exalted, said about Pharaoh: ﴿He will lead his people on the Day of Resurrection﴾ [Hud: 98], meaning he will precede them into the Fire.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 44, verse 43:

﴿Indeed, the tree of zaqqum, the food of the sinful, like molten brass, it boils in the bellies, like the boiling of scalding water.﴾

Al-Haqq, glorified and exalted is He, gives us here a picture of the food of the people of the Fire, may God protect us, and in another place He gives us a picture of their drink, because food and drink here are the foundation of life. Their food is the zaqqum, which is a small tree, foul-smelling, and its taste is bitter.

As for its form, He, glorified is He, said about it in another verse: ﴿Its shoots are as if they were the heads of devils﴾ [al-Saffat: 65], and this is a comparison that conveys the intended meaning precisely, for the purpose is to show its ugliness and the repulsiveness of its appearance.

For this reason we find some orientalists objecting to this comparison, saying: how can one compare the unknown with the unknown, since no one has seen the heads of devils, whereas the principle in comparison is to liken the unknown to the known so that the clarification may be complete?

They say this because they know nothing of the miraculous nature of the Qur'an and its method of conveying meaning. If we were to hold a competition among the caricaturists of the world and said to them: draw us a picture of the devil, each one would draw it according to his own imagination of ugliness in his view.

Thus we would have many pictures, all of them ugly though they differ, because ugliness has different colours, and what is hideous to one person may not be so to another, just as the standards of beauty are found to be relative among people. For example, some see beauty in thin lips, and another sees it in thick lips.

Likewise the standards of ugliness differ in the human mind, and the image that frightens one person may not frighten another. So the Al-Haqq, glorified is He, by this image willed to spread its ugliness and hideousness, and to make it ugly in a general way that encompasses every aspect of ugliness and hideousness among the various people.

So then: the indefiniteness here is better, because it lets you go in conceiving ugliness every way you can, and therefore we may say that the indefiniteness here is the utmost clarity and the very essence of exposition.

So then: it is a tree that is repulsive in its form, its taste and its smell. Then he adds to that by comparing its taste to ﴿like molten brass, it boils in the bellies﴾ [al-Dukhan: 45]. Al-muhl is: molten metal that has reached the utmost heat, or it is boiling oil...

The meaning of ﴿it boils in the bellies﴾ [al-Dukhan: 45] is that its temperature, God protect us, does not drop by drinking it. For example, when we drink tea hot, we feel the sting of heat in the mouth as we take it, but when it reaches the stomach this temperature drops.

As for the zaqqum, God protect us, it keeps boiling even in their bellies, ﴿like the boiling of scalding water﴾ [al-Dukhan: 46].

Like the boiling of water that has reached its utmost degree, and its heat has become intense.

﴿This...﴾ [Al-Dukhan: 50] That is, the punishment that befell them. ﴿This is what you used to doubt﴾ [Al-Dukhan: 50], meaning: you used to have doubts about it and deny it, and now it has become a reality that has come to pass.

Then Allah, glorified and exalted is He, mentions the opposite category, saying:

﴿Indeed, the righteous...﴾.

Bringing together opposites is one of the methods of Qur'anic expression, because contrast makes the image clearer.

The Arab poet was also aware of this meaning, and said:

*So the face is like the dawn, white,
and the hair is like the night, black.*

*Two opposites, when brought together, are beautiful,
and the opposite reveals the beauty of its opposite.*

Among this is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss, and indeed, the wicked will be in the Blazing Fire﴾ [Al-Infitar: 13-14]. It is for you to draw the comparison and make your choice. Therefore, after He told us of the fate of the criminals and the torments He has prepared for them, He mentions the fate of the God-fearing (al-muttaqun) and the bliss He has prepared for them.

﴿Indeed, the God-fearing will be in a secure station﴾ [Al-Dukhan: 51]. The muttaqi (the God-conscious person) is one who places between himself and the attributes of Allah's majesty a shield of the attributes of majesty, such as the Subduer, the Compeller, the Avenger, the One of severe punishment. So, O believer, make between yourself and these attributes of Allah a shield, for you cannot bear the attributes of majesty of Allah.

Therefore He says: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah...﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 278], and He says: ﴿Then fear the Fire whose fuel is men and stones...﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 24], because it is one of the soldiers of the attributes of subjugation and majesty. So, they both carry the same meaning.

As for His saying ﴿in a secure station﴾ [Al-Dukhan: 51]: the maqam is the place of residence, or the dwelling in which you live, which has parts; you sit in one part and sleep in another, and so on. But among the most important qualities of a dwelling is that it be secure, so that you feel safe in it for yourself and your property.

Therefore, when we plan to build a residential city, we must first provide the requirements of security for its residents. The first of these is that it be far from the grazing grounds of wild beasts and predatory animals, and likewise safe from thieves or traitors, that is, from the human who infiltrates your home and disturbs you, such that when you are sleeping or sitting, you have to get up and stand before him.

So a secure place, or a secure station, is one where you feel safe from everything. Thus, security in the maqam (the station, with the vowel fatha on the mim) is above security in the muqam (the residence, with the vowel damma on the mim). Therefore our master Ibrahim prayed to his Lord: ﴿My Lord, make this a secure city...﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 126], meaning general security, as is required of any city.

When He had granted him this, he prayed for special security, saying: ﴿My Lord, make this land secure...﴾ [Ibrahim: 35]. Then Allah, glory be to Him, gave him a security above all of this, namely the sanctity of the Sacred House, saying: ﴿Whoever enters it shall be secure﴾ [Al 'Imran: 97], to the extent that a man would meet the killer of his father there and not approach him, out of reverence for the sanctity of the House.

Therefore, when the events occurred at the Sacred House, when gunfire was fired within it and those who were secure were terrified, there emerged among us some atheists who seized the opportunity and began to cast doubt on His saying: ﴿Whoever enters it shall be secure﴾ [Al 'Imran: 97], because what happened seemed to contradict this verse.

Here we should distinguish between two methods of Qur'anic expression. His saying ﴿Whoever enters it shall be secure﴾ [Al 'Imran: 97] does not mean giving information that whoever enters it is secure; rather, what is meant is: I am asking you to make secure whoever enters it. It is a legal command which may be obeyed, so that we make secure whoever enters, and it may be disobeyed, so that we terrify whoever enters.

So the verse contains a talabi insha' (a demand-type utterance; insha' is non-declarative speech), and it is not a khabar (a declarative statement). It is known that a khabar admits of truth or falsehood, whereas insha' admits neither truth nor falsehood.

Among this is His saying: ﴿Evil women are for evil men, and evil men for evil women; good women are for good men, and good men for good women...﴾ [An-Nur: 26]. Some understand the verse as a report from Allah that evil women must be for evil men, then see in the reality of society something different, and so doubt the truth of the verse.

But the meaning is otherwise. The meaning is legislative: give evil women to evil men, and give good women to good men. This is a legal command which some may obey and others may disobey.

The wisdom and correctness lie in following Allah's commands, so that equality is achieved between the two and the balance of married life is maintained. If we imagine a good man marrying an evil woman, what happens? Discord and incompatibility occur; then the husband reproaches her for her past and humiliates her for her previous misdeeds. But if an evil man takes an evil woman, compatibility results; and if he says to her, "You were such-and-such," she replies, "And you were such-and-such."

So: Allah has imposed cosmic matters which never change and which the reality of life never contradicts, and He has imposed legal matters (shar'i) left to the choice of the responsible person (mukallaf), who either acts upon them or does not. This verse and its like are not a cosmic decree; they are a legal command, as if Allah were saying: O you who believe in a legal command, carry out this statement.

His saying ﴿in gardens and springs﴾ [Al-Dukhan: 52]: the jannat are orchards and gardens, which to the Arabs are something beautiful and a great blessing. If security is among the necessities, then gardens and springs are among the luxuries and additional bounty.

He said ﴿and springs﴾ because gardens must have springs to water their crops and nourish their fruit. And after He guaranteed them security and the luxury of life, He guarantees them fine clothing: ﴿They will wear green silk and brocade, facing one another﴾ [Al-Dukhan: 53].

Sundus is fine silk, and istabraq is thick, heavy silk. This also indicates luxury and riyash (finery), which denotes ostentation. For clothing includes what is necessary, which covers the nakedness, and includes riyash, because they used to adorn clothing with ostrich feathers. Therefore they still say to this day, "(so-and-so is mutarrish)," meaning one who is adorned with finery, that is, he has luxury in his living.

He says: ﴿O children of Adam, We have sent down to you clothing to cover your nakedness, and as finery; but the clothing of righteousness, that is best...﴾ [Al-A'raf: 26].

So these are three kinds of clothing: necessary clothing that covers the nakedness; clothing of luxury and adornment; and the clothing of taqwa (God-consciousness), which is the best and most excellent of them. For the most you get from clothing is covering your nakedness in this world and appearing in a good form among people. It is clothing limited to your lifetime in this world. A person may die immediately after coming out of his mother's womb, so he has no share of this clothing and has no nakedness to be covered.

As for the clothing of taqwa, it is an adornment for you in this world and salvation for you in the Hereafter, the abode of permanence and the abode of eternity. Therefore He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And the clothing of righteousness, that is best...﴾ [Al-A'raf: 26].

We note that Allah, after mentioning the punishment He has prepared for the disbelievers, mentioned what He has prepared for the believers who affirm His messengers, and made the Day of Resurrection a day of separation between them: ﴿Indeed, the Day of Decision is the appointed time for them all﴾ [Al-Dukhan: 40].

Separation occurs between two things that are united in one matter and differ in another. The believers and the disbelievers are united in existence, in the bounty of lordship, and in enjoying the blessings of Allah in this world.
