So the meaning has moved from the matter of marriage that we know to the intimacy of beauty, which is the summit of the pleasures we know. It is not necessarily that very act, because in the Hereafter we will be created a new creation, different from this creation we live in, as evidence that you eat in Paradise and do not relieve yourself.

Accordingly, the meaning is the pairing of two, regardless of male or female, because the pleasure there is the pleasure of looking, the pleasure of conversation, and the pleasure of companionship through values other than those we know now.

His saying ﴿with wide-eyed maidens﴾ [Al-Dukhan: 54]: ḥūr is the plural of ḥawrā' (a woman of Paradise), and ḥawar is a quality of the eye meaning intense whiteness and intense blackness in the eye. 'Ῑn is the plural of 'aynā', one with large eyes together with their beauty.

If you look at her mouth, you would find it is twice as small as her eye. Therefore they describe the beauty of the mouth as like the ring of Solomon. You may imagine this sight.

Since a man's marriage to a woman is among the greatest pleasures of this world, and both man and woman eagerly desire it when they reach maturity, Allah made it among the pleasures of the Hereafter, but in a purer form. He made it among the pleasures of the Hereafter regardless of that very sexual act. The matter is companionship with what you used to regard as a blessing in this world. But in the Hereafter there are other standards: in the Hereafter He will purify for you things from the irritants that existed in this world.

Have you considered, for example, the wine, honey and milk of this world? You will have them in the Hereafter, but after We purify them for you from what spoils them. He made the wine of the Hereafter a delight for drinkers, whereas the wine of this world has no delight in it. He made the milk whose taste never changes, and He made the water unstinking.

Likewise, He made marriage pure of its impurities and irritants of this world. Even the spouses of the world, when Allah gathers them in the abode of His mercy in Paradise, the husband finds his wife in a different form, for Allah purifies her for him and cleanses her of the faults for which he used to reproach her in this world.

So if she was, for example, not beautiful, he finds her as beautiful as women can be; and if she was in this world ill-tongued, he finds her in the best of states, because Allah will bring them into being in a new creation: ﴿Indeed, We have produced them with a special production, and made them virgins, loving, of equal age, for the companions of the right﴾ [Al-Waqi'ah: 35-38]. And He said: ﴿and purified spouses...﴾ [Al 'Imran: 15].

From this bi we understand that it is a marriage different from the one we know in this world between man and woman, and that it is far from that very matter, because the afterlife has a different bliss and other standards than what we know in this world.

The phrase (wide-eyed maidens) draws the mind to the pleasure of looking and delighting in it, as a person looks at a friend he loves. If he is content and satisfied with this blessing, then welcome; and if looking does not satisfy him, then in Paradise there is what souls desire and what delights the eyes.

Bringing together opposites is one of the methods of Qur'anic expression, because contrast makes the image clearer.

The Arab poet was also aware of this meaning, and said:

*So the face is like the dawn, white,
and the hair is like the night, black.*

*Two opposites, when brought together, are beautiful,
and the opposite reveals the beauty of its opposite.*

Among this is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in bliss, and indeed, the wicked will be in the Blazing Fire﴾ [Al-Infitar: 13-14]. It is for you to draw the comparison and make your choice. Therefore, after He told us of the fate of the criminals and the torments He has prepared for them, He mentions the fate of the God-fearing (al-muttaqun) and the bliss He has prepared for them.

﴿Indeed, the God-fearing will be in a secure station﴾ [Al-Dukhan: 51]. The muttaqi (the God-conscious person) is one who places between himself and the attributes of Allah's majesty a shield of the attributes of majesty, such as the Subduer, the Compeller, the Avenger, the One of severe punishment. So, O believer, make between yourself and these attributes of Allah a shield, for you cannot bear the attributes of majesty of Allah.

Therefore He says: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah...﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 278], and He says: ﴿Then fear the Fire whose fuel is men and stones...﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 24], because it is one of the soldiers of the attributes of subjugation and majesty. So, they both carry the same meaning.

As for His saying ﴿in a secure station﴾ [Al-Dukhan: 51]: the maqam is the place of residence, or the dwelling in which you live, which has parts; you sit in one part and sleep in another, and so on. But among the most important qualities of a dwelling is that it be secure, so that you feel safe in it for yourself and your property.

Therefore, when we plan to build a residential city, we must first provide the requirements of security for its residents. The first of these is that it be far from the grazing grounds of wild beasts and predatory animals, and likewise safe from thieves or traitors, that is, from the human who infiltrates your home and disturbs you, such that when you are sleeping or sitting, you have to get up and stand before him.

So a secure place, or a secure station, is one where you feel safe from everything. Thus, security in the maqam (the station, with the vowel fatha on the mim) is above security in the muqam (the residence, with the vowel damma on the mim). Therefore our master Ibrahim prayed to his Lord: ﴿My Lord, make this a secure city...﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 126], meaning general security, as is required of any city.

Here we should distinguish between two methods of Qur'anic expression. His saying ﴿Whoever enters it shall be secure﴾ [Al 'Imran: 97] does not mean giving information that whoever enters it is secure; rather, what is meant is: I am asking you to make secure whoever enters it. It is a legal command which may be obeyed, so that we make secure whoever enters, and it may be disobeyed, so that we terrify whoever enters.

So the verse contains a talabi insha' (a demand-type utterance; insha' is non-declarative speech), and it is not a khabar (a declarative statement). It is known that a khabar admits of truth or falsehood, whereas insha' admits neither truth nor falsehood.

Among this is His saying: ﴿Evil women are for evil men, and evil men for evil women; good women are for good men, and good men for good women...﴾ [An-Nur: 26]. But the meaning is otherwise. The meaning is legislative: give evil women to evil men, and give good women to good men. This is a legal command which some may obey and others may disobey.

The wisdom and correctness lie in following Allah's commands, so that equality is achieved between the two and the balance of married life is maintained. If we imagine a good man marrying an evil woman, what happens? Discord and incompatibility occur; then the husband reproaches her for her past and humiliates her for her previous misdeeds. But if an evil man takes an evil woman, compatibility results; and if he says to her, "You were such-and-such," she replies, "And you were such-and-such."

So: Allah has imposed cosmic matters which never change and which the reality of life never contradicts, and He has imposed legal matters (shar'i) left to the choice of the responsible person (mukallaf), who either acts upon them or does not. This verse and its like are not a cosmic decree; they are a legal command, as if Allah were saying: O you who believe in a legal command, carry out this statement.

He said ﴿and springs﴾ because gardens must have springs to water their crops and nourish their fruit. And after He guaranteed them security and the luxury of life, He guarantees them fine clothing: ﴿They will wear green silk and brocade, facing one another﴾ [Al-Dukhan: 53].

Sundus is fine silk, and istabraq is thick, heavy silk. This also indicates luxury and riyash (finery), which denotes ostentation. For clothing includes what is necessary, which covers the nakedness, and includes riyash, because they used to adorn clothing with ostrich feathers. Therefore they still say to this day, "(so-and-so is mutarrish)," meaning one who is adorned with finery, that is, he has luxury in his living.

He says: ﴿O children of Adam, We have sent down to you clothing to cover your nakedness, and as finery; but the clothing of righteousness, that is best...﴾ [Al-A'raf: 26].

So these are three kinds of clothing: necessary clothing that covers the nakedness; clothing of luxury and adornment; and the clothing of taqwa (God-consciousness), which is the best and most excellent of them. For the most you get from clothing is covering your nakedness in this world and appearing in a good form among people. It is clothing limited to your lifetime in this world. A person may die immediately after coming out of his mother's womb, so he has no share of this clothing and has no nakedness to be covered.

As for the clothing of taqwa, it is an adornment for you in this world and salvation for you in the Hereafter, the abode of permanence and the abode of eternity. Therefore He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿And the clothing of righteousness, that is best...﴾ [Al-A'raf: 26].

The believers and the disbelievers are united in existence, in the bounty of lordship, and in enjoying the blessings of Allah in this world. Allah has made the necessities of life available to all: water, air and food.

They are equal in this, because He is the Lord of them all and their Creator, and He is the One who summoned them into existence; so He must guarantee for them the necessities of their life. But He arranged these necessities in degrees. When He spoke of clothing, He said: ﴿O children of Adam...﴾ [Al-A'raf: 26], and did not single out the believers, because this gift is a gift of divinity. ﴿We have sent down to you clothing to cover your nakedness...﴾ [Al-A'raf: 26]. So they are partners in the necessary clothing that covers nakedness, and in finery which indicates splendour and adornment beyond necessity; and all of these are among the pleasures of worldly life. The matter in the Hereafter is different. For the disbelievers is the tree of Zaqqum, which boils in the bellies like the boiling of scalding water; but the God-fearing are in gardens and springs, in a secure station.

The words (sundus) and (istabraq) are of Persian origin that entered Arabic, and the Noble Qur'an used them as Arabic words that passed on the tongues of the Arabs. Therefore the orientalists paused at these words, and at similar ones such as qistas (the balance) and others. But there is no objection to a language using words from another language.

Since these words entered the speech of the Arab, he used them and understood their meaning until they became part of the language through which he communicates, what prevents their use as Arabic words? For example, we today use the word (bank), which is not Arabic, and perhaps we find it lighter and more graceful than the Arabic word masraf.

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi (surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66)) on surah 44, verse 55–56:

The meaning of ﴿They call for﴾ [Ad-Dukhan: 55] is they ask for. ﴿Therein﴾ [Ad-Dukhan: 55] means: in Paradise. If you say: why would they ask for it, when in Paradise a thing comes to you the moment you want it? The answer given is that the matter concerns eating: the natural or necessary kind of eating, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿and the flesh of birds, of whatever they desire﴾ [Al-Waqi'ah: 21].

After eating, one wishes for fruit for enjoyment (tafakkuh), and as long as your soul desires it, it comes to you, even if it is ﴿of every fruit﴾ [Ad-Dukhan: 55], meaning: of every kind and every form. Any one of us, however great his worldly comfort, after his main meal eats one or two kinds of fruit. But in Paradise they call for every fruit, meaning: "O Lord, bring us every kind of fruit."

Here we ask: what stomach can bear and contain all of this? What soul can receive all these similar things? By Allah, if we were in this world, we would suffer problems in the stomach, in the intestines, and elsewhere. In Paradise, however, the matter is different.

Look at the end of the verse, ﴿secure﴾ [Ad-Dukhan: 55]. The word "secure" arrives to remove every astonishment and wonder: there you eat everything you love, and eat whatever your soul desires.

It is a secure eating, free from the dangers of food that you knew in this world, a food that your Lord, Mighty and Majestic, prepared for you and purified from everything that spoils it, and from every defect of food that you knew in this world. Its purity is sufficient proof that you may eat from it as much as you wish and you do not defecate. Thus: the blessing of Paradise is refined, pure, free from impurities and from hardships.

As for His saying, glory be to Him: ﴿They taste not therein death, except the first death﴾ [Ad-Dukhan: 56], meaning: in Paradise too. Paradise is a container, and there is no death in Paradise. So how is the exception ﴿except the first death﴾ [Ad-Dukhan: 56] made within it? The meaning is that they do not taste death in Paradise: death, for them, ended with the first death that occurred to them in this world, while in Paradise there is no death.

The word ﴿they taste﴾ [Ad-Dukhan: 56] makes the sense of taste, which is confined to the tongue and the area around it responsible for tasting things, a general sense throughout the whole body, encompassing all the other senses.

As He, glory be to Him, said about the torment of the people of the Fire: ﴿Taste it! Indeed, you are the mighty, the noble﴾ [Ad-Dukhan: 49]. He tastes the torment not with his tongue, but with every limb of his. And He, glory be to Him, said in another verse: ﴿So Allah made them taste the envelopment of hunger and fear for what they had been doing﴾ [An-Nahl: 112]. Here He made the sense of taste like a garment that encompasses the whole body, as if every part of his body tastes the flavour of torment.

As for His saying: ﴿and He protected them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire﴾ [Ad-Dukhan: 56], meaning: first, before this bliss, He protected them from the punishment of the Blazing Fire. Protection from punishment precedes their entry into Paradise and comes before it, because the rule, as we have said, is: clearing away before adorning (at-takhliyah qabla at-tahliyah). Therefore He, glory be to Him, said: ﴿So whoever is drawn away from the Fire and admitted into Paradise has certainly succeeded﴾ [Ali 'Imran: 185].

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 44, verse 57:

﴿As a bounty from your Lord. That is the supreme triumph.﴾

Meaning: Paradise and the bliss in it, and before that, protection from punishment, all of this is ﴿a bounty from your Lord﴾ [al-Dukhan: 57], that is, a favour from Him, may He be glorified, toward us, and a gift of generosity from Him to His creation, not in return for their deeds.

This matter is one on which the scholars differ, because the Almighty said in another verse: ﴿Enter Paradise for what you used to do﴾ [al-Nahl: 32], and He also said: ﴿Say: "In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy, in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate."﴾ [Yunus: 58].

So we have verses that speak of Allah's bounty and verses that speak of deeds, and the enemies of Islam are sure to seize upon such matters, trying to cast doubt on the words of the Lord of the worlds and to accuse Him of contradiction. Exalted is Allah above that, most high.

To clarify this matter, we say: when you take care of your child, spend on him, and give him lessons so that he excels, do you do that for his benefit or for yours? And when he excels, you bring him a reward that motivates him to continue in success. So you have taken upon yourself burdens and expenses that do not return to you, but return to your son.

In the same way, the Almighty deals with His creation. Allah created us and created for us the means of our life, then He gave us the way (manhaj) and rewarded us for it, so we benefit by remaining upright upon it in this world and by reward for it in the Hereafter.

The Almighty does this while He is free of need of us. To Him belong all the attributes of perfection before He created this creation. So obedience does not benefit Him, and disobedience does not harm Him.

Beware lest you think that by your obedience to Allah and your worship of Him you support His throne, may He be exalted, or add to His creation. You are the one who benefits, first and last, from the way of Allah, and it is an honour for you to be affiliated with this way and to be a servant of Allah, exalted is He.

Therefore there came in the sacred hadith (hadith qudsi): "O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were upon the most wicked heart of one man among you, that would not decrease My dominion in anything. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, were upon the most pious heart of one man among you, that would not increase My dominion in anything. O My servants, if the first of you and the last of you, your humans and your jinn, gathered in one plain and each of you asked Me for what he wished, and I gave each his request, that would not decrease what is with Me except as a needle decreases the sea when it is dipped into it. That is because I am Generous, Glorious, Self-Sufficient (Wajid); My giving is speech, and My punishment is speech; My command, when I desire a thing, is only that I say to it, 'Be,' and it is."

So: the obligation that comes to us from Allah the Exalted brings Allah no benefit whatsoever; its benefit returns to us. Had we taken the matter by reason alone, we would have said that it was incumbent upon us to pay the price. Thus the reward for obedience is pure bounty from Allah; indeed, the mere legislation and the way which Allah has charged you with is pure bounty from Him, glorified is He.

Therefore the Exalted said: ﴿As a bounty from your Lord. That is the supreme triumph﴾ [al-Dukhan: 57]. The supreme triumph is that when I walk in accordance with the way of Allah, I benefit from it in this world and am rewarded for it in the Hereafter.

As for His saying, glorified is He: ﴿Enter Paradise for what you used to do﴾ [al-Nahl: 32], they said: it means "because of your righteous deeds." Righteous deeds are not a price for Paradise, but a cause of entering it. Our master, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), clarified this matter when he said: "None of you will enter Paradise by his deeds." They said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even I, unless Allah covers me with His mercy."

In the light of this hadith we understand His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Say: "In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy, in that let them rejoice; it is better than what they accumulate."﴾ [Yunus: 58].

Here Allah, glorified is He, returns to address His Prophet (ﷺ) and to explain His blessing upon him. Among these blessings is that He, glorified is He, made the Qur'an easy for him, so that he recites it in a clear Arabic tongue. The pronoun in ﴿يَسَّرْنَاهُ..﴾ [al-Dukhan: 58] refers to the Qur'an, as shown by His words ﴿بِلِسَانِكَ..﴾ [al-Dukhan: 58]. This is a linguistic provision, since Allah made it in the tongue and language of Arabic, which is the tongue of the Messenger (ﷺ) and the language through which he speaks.

His words ﴿لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ﴾ [al-Dukhan: 58] show that it is in your tongue and in the tongue of your people. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿وَمَآ أَرْسَلْنَا مِن رَّسُولٍ إِلاَّ بِلِسَانِ قَوْمِهِ﴾ [Ibrahim: 4]. So it is in your tongue for conveying (tabligh), and in their tongue for receiving and taking it in, and then for further conveying, because they are the ones who will carry out the task of conveying after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Commentary of al-Sha'rawi (Tafsir al-Sha'rawi, surahs 1-53, fragments of 54-66) on surah 44, verse 59:

فَارْتَقِبْ.. "So await" – i.e., wait: إِنَّهُمْ مُّرْتَقِبُونَ "indeed they too are waiting." So what is the Messenger of Allah waiting for, and what are the disbelievers waiting for? The Messenger of Allah is the bearer of a call and of guidance; he came with a light by which he guides these people, while they oppose his call and show hostility to him, wishing to extinguish this light. He is eager for them and loves their guidance despite their harming him and their mockery of him, to the point that he almost destroys himself in the cause of his call.

Therefore his Lord often addressed him, consoling him and lightening his burden, informing him: ﴿Your duty is only to convey (the message)﴾ [al-Shura: 48]; ﴿Perhaps you would kill yourself with grief that they do not become believers﴾ [al-Shu'ara: 3].

And He said: ﴿We know that what they say grieves you; but it is not you they deny, rather it is the signs of Allah that the wrongdoers reject﴾ [al-An'am: 33]. Meaning: do not grieve, O Muhammad, over what they say about you, for they love you, esteem you, and know your truthfulness and your station; you are too high in their eyes to lie to them. But the matter is that they reject My signs, so the matter rests with Me.

The phrase فَارْتَقِبْ "so await" came twice in this surah here, and in His saying, glorified is He: ﴿So await the day when the sky brings a clear smoke﴾ [al-Dukhan: 10], when the Messenger of Allah prayed against them and said: "O Allah, tighten Your grip upon Mudar, and make it for them years like the years of Joseph."

So there befell them such drought and famine that they ate carrion and al-'ilhiz (a paste of blood and hair), and they cried out, calling upon Allah to remove it from them. Allah knew that if He removed it from them, they would return to what they were upon, denying His Messenger.

Therefore Allah addressed His Messenger with His saying: ﴿And whether We show you some of what We promise them, or We take you (in death), to Us they will be returned﴾ [Ghafir: 77].

So the meaning of فَارْتَقِبْ is: wait for what punishment will descend upon them, because they are awaiting what would relieve them of you and free them from your call. Therefore our Lord, glorified and exalted is He, teaches His Messenger how to argue with them, saying to them: ﴿Say: Do you await for us anything but one of the two best outcomes? And we await for you that Allah will afflict you with a punishment from Him, or at our hands. So await; indeed we are with you among those who await﴾ [al-Tawba: 52].

Meaning: say to them, O Muhammad: you wait for us one of the two best outcomes, either victory over you, or that we die as martyrs. If we are victorious over you, the way of Allah will rise and prevail; and if we die, we are martyrs, living with our Lord, being provided for. And we await for you that Allah afflict you with a punishment from Him or at our hands. Thus: we await for you evil for you, and you await for us good for us.
